function.arguments: {"observation": "The `channel` variable is not randomly assigned: the email campaign was deliberately targeted at existing high-value customers (e.g., `loyal` and `returning`), while `paid_search` was not. The cross-tabulation shows a strong imbalance: email has 132 loyal and 134 returning customers, while paid_search has only 26 loyal and 153 returning. The `loyal` segment is overrepresented in email, which has higher inherent conversion rates. A raw comparison of conversion rates between channels is confounded by customer segment.", "implication": "The raw difference in conversion rates (email minus paid_search) is not a valid estimate of the causal effect of the email campaign. It reflects both the campaign effect and the pre-existing differences in customer segment. To estimate the true campaign effect, we must control for `customer_segment` — either by stratifying, standardizing, or modeling the relationship. Otherwise, we risk attributing differences due to targeting to the campaign itself."}
function.name: note_finding
